This document is the working task list for the RestoreDART results, converted from
the plain-text `TODO` file. It has two parts: the caveats that apply to every figure
and table in `2_make_DART_results.Rmd`, and the outstanding analysis and reporting
tasks, grouped by theme rather than by the order in which they were written down.

**Review status.** Every task below has been checked against the results document as it
currently stands. Items that the current results address adequately are ~~struck
through~~ and followed by an italic *Addressed:* note saying where the work lives.
Items that are only partially covered carry a *Partly addressed:* note saying what
exists and what is still missing, and items with no coverage carry an *Outstanding:*
note. A few items resolved by a decision to **not** do the work are struck as well,
with the note recording where that decision is documented.

**How locations are cited.** The earlier version of this list gave line numbers in a
single 716-line `2_make_DART_results.Rmd`. That file no longer exists in that form: the
report has been split into a driver (`2_make_DART_results.Rmd` - setup, constants, the
cross-objective compilation chunks and the hand-written interpretation) and a template
(`_objective_block.Rmd`), which the driver's `objective_blocks` chunk expands once per
element of `summaries` with `knit_expand()` and renders with `knit_child()`. A line
number is therefore no longer a unique location - the template's lines are rendered
once per objective - so every note below cites a **file and chunk label** instead.
Template chunk labels come out as `results-X_Y`, where `X` is the objective's index and
`Y` counts chunks within that objective's block from 0; a note that says
`_objective_block.Rmd`, chunk `results-X_18` means that chunk in every objective's
section. Chunk labels are stable under editing in a way line numbers are not.

The report now covers **five** objective x cover response combinations, not one:
`decrease_afg` (AFG), `decrease_shr` (SHR), `decrease_tre` (TRE), `increase_pfg` (PFG)
and `increase_shr` (SHR). Several notes below have been rewritten because a task that
was previously only drafted for `decrease_afg` now runs for all five.

Of the 22 task entries, 15 are struck in full, along with all four of the collaborator
sub-questions; 2 are partly addressed, 4 are outstanding, and 1 (the de-prioritisation
of publication graphics) is a standing priority note rather than a task. The four fully
outstanding items are the model `.Rmd` split, time metrics in the summary table, a
stability-over-time metric, and re-checking the written interpretations against the
figures that were reoriented from raw-positive to intended in this revision.

**Closed since the last revision of this list.** The largest one is the **late-year
sample-size cut-off**, which had been the longest-standing outstanding item and is now
implemented as `min_year_n` plus `truncate_late_years()`; its item below records what it
removed. Alongside it: the three per-section `summarize_sig_effect()` figures now report
the **intended** effect rather than the raw positive one; a **depopulated-level** filter
was added so a treatment or ecoregion thinned across surviving cells can be dropped
rather than only reported; the compiled summary table is now also written in the
reporting spreadsheet's **column order** via `summary_template_map()`; the
significantly-shifting **heatmap** was removed from each section; the hand-written
**interpretation section moved to the end** of the report; and the polygon-count
histogram's axis was fixed (it had been requesting one break per integer, rendering 39
labels as a run of digits). The weighting question is settled and struck. The
"Polygon count by year since treatment" figure was checked against an independent
recount of distinct polygon x year pairs and is correct as drawn.

## Caveats and considerations

These apply to all of the figures and tables in the current results document and
should be restated wherever those results are presented.

- **Objectives are not mutually exclusive.** The objective groupings count a pixel as
  part of an objective if that pixel fell within *any* part of the defined objective.
  Multi-objective treatments are therefore included in several objective groupings at
  once, and substantial parts of the dataset are counted more than once across the
  figures and tables. Counts and percentages should be read as per-objective summaries,
  not as a partition of the dataset. *This caveat is now quantified rather than just
  stated: the co-occurrence table in `_objective_block.Rmd`, chunk `results-X_22` reports
  how many of that objective's pixels carried no second objective and how many carried
  each of the others, and the driver's `compile_overlap` chunk stacks all five
  objectives' versions into one table.*
- **Objective/response pairings are restricted.** An objective/response combination is
  only included if the response variable is the same cover type as the objective's
  target cover (for example, `decrease_afg` paired with the differenced AFG response).
  The single exception is bare ground, which is shown in combination with every
  objective because it is informative regardless of which cover type was targeted.

## Time effects

This is the largest open block of work. The overall aim is to describe *when* after
treatment an effect appears, how long it persists, and how confident we can be in
that timing given the available sample.

  *Addressed: `_objective_block.Rmd`, chunk `results-X_18`. `sig_by_year` tabulates

## Sample size and polygon standardisation

- **Standardise polygons on the basis of their time series.** Check that a small number
  of polygons with unusually long records are not extending the overall time series and
  dominating the visualisations.
  *Partly addressed, and further along than at the last revision. The diagnostic is in
  `_objective_block.Rmd`, chunk `results-X_11`, which plots for each year since treatment
  how many distinct polygons contribute at least one pixel - that figure has been checked
  against an independent recount of distinct polygon x year pairs and is correct as drawn
  (it peaks at each objective's true polygon total and declines monotonically).
  `poly_best_worst` in chunk `results-X_21` also records `n_years` per polygon.*

  *Action is now taken on the diagnostic at the SERIES level: the late-year truncation
  above cuts the record where the per-year sample size gives out, so the per-year figures
  no longer run to the full extent of the longest-record polygons regardless of how few
  remain. What is still missing is action at the POLYGON level - no individual polygon is
  trimmed or reweighted on the basis of its own record length, so a handful of
  long-record polygons can still be the only contributors to the last retained years.
  The five objectives' records also remain of unequal length (28, 33, 33, 33 and 30
  post-treatment years before truncation, 26 and 32 after it for the two truncated
  objectives), so the x axis of the cross-objective peak figure spans a different amount
  of data in each panel.*
- ~~**Consider a sample size cut-off for polygons after a given year**, so that years
  supported by only a handful of polygons are not plotted or summarised as though they
  were as well supported as the early years.~~
  *Addressed. `min_year_n` is set in the driver's `setup` chunk, keyed per objective
  exactly like `min_txeco_n` (both now resolve through the same `keyed_threshold()`), and
  applied by `truncate_late_years()` in `_objective_block.Rmd`, chunk `results-X_6`. It
  **truncates** rather than excluding individual years: the first year below the
  threshold is found and that year plus every year after it is dropped, whether or not a
  later year clears the threshold again. That is the right shape for this data because
  the per-year sample size falls monotonically as polygons leave the post-treatment
  record, so a failing year marks where the record stops supporting a comparison and a
  later year that clears it is a blip inside an already-unreliable tail.*

  *The filter runs last of the three, after both spatial filters, so the per-year counts
  it tests are the ones the figures are actually drawn from. Its effect is recorded per
  objective in the `compile_filter_log` table (`Min. … Pixels per Year`, `Truncated From
  Year`, `# Years Dropped`), and each section states in prose where its own series was
  cut, so the truncation is visible rather than silent - which was the condition attached
  to this item.*

  *What it removes at the current setting (`min_year_n = c(default = 10)`,
  `year_trunc_metric = 'significant'`): `decrease_afg` is cut at year 27, losing 2 years
  and 0.10% of its pixels, so its series ends at 26; `decrease_shr` is cut at year 33,
  losing 1 year and 0.06%; `decrease_tre`, `increase_pfg` and `increase_shr` are not
  truncated at all. Modest, and deliberately so - see the open question below.*

  *One thing this item's earlier evidence got wrong, worth recording because it
  determines whether the filter does anything: the threshold cannot usefully be a
  **total**-pixel count. The per-year totals stay in the hundreds to the end of every
  objective's record (the smallest is 44 pixels, `decrease_afg` years 27-28), so any
  small total-pixel threshold truncates nothing. `year_trunc_metric` therefore defaults
  to `'significant'` - significant pixels in that year - which is the quantity the
  problem is about, since `mean_effect_by_year()` and `peak_effect_year()` average over
  significant pixels only. Setting it to `'pixels'` gives the exact analogue of
  `min_txeco_n` and, at any threshold near 10, does nothing.*

  *Still open, and now a narrower question than before: the threshold **value**. At 10
  significant pixels the filter removes the years where almost nothing was significant
  but leaves the small-n peaks that motivated the item - `decrease_shr`'s positive peak
  rested on a single significant pixel at year 27, which survives a per-year threshold of
  10 because that year had enough significant pixels in total across both directions. A
  threshold in the low hundreds would remove most of the small-n peaks, at the cost of
  cutting several objectives back by a decade or more. That is a judgement about how much
  record to give up, not a defect, and it is a one-line edit to `min_year_n` now that the
  mechanism exists. A per-year **x direction** threshold inside `mean_effect_by_year()`
  would be the sharper instrument if the peaks specifically are the concern.*

  *Evidence, September 2026, from runs of the pipeline against the full input file
  (9,094,508 rows). The problem is now visible across all five objectives rather than
  inferred from one. `peak_effect_year()` reports these peaks:*

  | Objective (cover) | Direction | Peak year | Mean effect | SE | n sig. pixels | Last year |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `decrease_afg` (AFG) | negative | 18 | -43.26 | 1.79 | 132 | 26 |
  | `decrease_afg` (AFG) | positive | 25 | +28.78 | 3.53 | **10** | 26 |
  | `decrease_shr` (SHR) | negative | 1 | -21.51 | 0.26 | 2,487 | 33 |
  | `decrease_shr` (SHR) | positive | 27 | +14.20 | - | **1** | 33 |
  | `decrease_tre` (TRE) | negative | 29 | -26.64 | 1.02 | 100 | 33 |
  | `decrease_tre` (TRE) | positive | 31 | +14.24 | 1.26 | **27** | 33 |
  | `increase_pfg` (PFG) | negative | 21 | -10.59 | 0.15 | 733 | 33 |
  | `increase_pfg` (PFG) | positive | 33 | +23.43 | 2.36 | **17** | 33 (censored) |
  | `increase_shr` (SHR) | negative | 2 | -11.94 | 0.11 | 3,034 | 30 |
  | `increase_shr` (SHR) | positive | 20 | +14.01 | 0.34 | 378 | 30 |

  *Seven of the ten reported peaks rest on fewer than 800 significant pixels and four on
  fewer than 30, against bins of 12,000 to 190,000 pixels elsewhere in the same
  objectives. The `decrease_shr` positive peak is the limiting case: a single significant
  pixel, so its SE is undefined and blank above. Every one of these small-n peaks is a
  positive (unintended) peak under a `decrease_*` objective or lands late in the record,
  which is exactly where the significant-pixel count has thinned. The `is_censored` flag
  catches only one of them - `increase_pfg` at year 33 - because it fires when the peak
  falls on the last observed year, not when it falls on a sparse interior one.*

  *Two things have changed since that evidence was written. First, the shortfall became
  legible rather than buried: `plot_peak_effect_summary()` prints the significant-pixel
  count beside every point, so a peak backed by one pixel is visibly different from one
  backed by three thousand. Second, and since this revision, it is partly **handled** -
  `min_year_n` and `truncate_late_years()` cut the series where the per-year sample size
  gives out, which is the mechanism this note had been asking for, and the filtering log
  reports what each objective lost. Note that the small-n precedent cited here no longer
  exists: the year × treatment × ecoregion heatmap that faded tiles under 30 pixels has
  been removed from the report.*

  *What the truncation does not yet do is protect the peaks specifically. It works on the
  per-year count across both directions, so a year with enough significant pixels in
  total can still yield a peak computed from one pixel in a single direction - which is
  exactly `decrease_shr`'s positive peak at year 27. The sharper instrument remains a
  minimum significant-pixel count per year × **direction** cell, applied inside
  `mean_effect_by_year()` so the peak table, the dashed peak lines, the per-objective
  figure and the compiled figure cannot disagree. The open question is unchanged in kind
  but narrower in scope: what value, and counted as pixels or polygons. A per-year
  threshold in the low hundreds would remove most of the small-n peaks above at the cost
  of cutting several objectives back by a decade, which is a judgement about how much
  record to give up rather than a defect to fix.*
- ~~**Add time sample size tables to the `.Rmd`.** Specifically, are sample sizes in the
  later years being reduced, and is that reduction affecting the results
  disproportionately? These tables are the evidence base for the cut-off decision
  above.~~
  *Addressed: four complementary views, all in `_objective_block.Rmd` except the last.
  Chunk `results-X_11` gives polygons contributing per year since treatment; chunk
  `results-X_18` carries an `n_pix` total-pixel column per year in `sig_by_year` and
  labels every bar in the stacked figure with both its group total and its per-direction
  significant counts; chunk `results-X_20` reports total pixels per year bin; and the
  driver's two new compiled figures print sample sizes directly on the figure -
  `compile_sig_by_bin_plot` labels each bar with its bin total and
  `compile_peak_effect_plot` labels each peak with the significant-pixel count behind it.
  Whether the late-year reduction is distorting the results is the judgement the cut-off
  item above still has to make, but the numbers needed to make it are now in the
  document, and for the peaks specifically they are on the figure rather than only in a
  table column.*

## Specific questions from collaborators

Cross-objective direction checks that KY asked for. Each of these looks at the
directions of the *non-target* functional groups when a given objective was the
management goal.

- ~~When decreasing tree cover was the goal, what do the AFG, SHR and PFG group
  directions look like?~~
- ~~When increasing PFG cover was the goal, what do the AFG directions look like?~~
- ~~When decreasing shrub cover was the goal, what do the AFG, PFG and TRE directions
  look like?~~
  *Addressed - all three now run and render. They live under the driver's
  *Cross-objective direction checks* heading, one chunk each
  (`results_total_tre`, `results_total_pfg`, `results_total_shr`), as
  `compare_related_directions()` calls on `combined_df`, each returning a table of
  percent significant and percent significant by direction for the named cover
  responses, plus a figure.*

  *These were previously written but left `eval = FALSE`, because the third call errored
  with `nrow(df) > 0 is not TRUE`. The cause was a misspelled objective: the call asked
  for `decrease_shb`, and the shrub objective in the input data is coded `decrease_shr`
  (matching the `SHR` `fun_group`, which is the uppercased suffix `split_by_objective()`
  pairs the two on). `grepl()` on the misspelled string matched no rows, so the function
  stopped on its own guard - which is the guard behaving correctly, since an empty result
  there means the filter was wrong rather than that the data is uninteresting. The
  spelling is fixed, the chunks are evaluated, and the error is recorded as a comment in
  the first of the three chunks so the same string is not reintroduced.*

  *Two caveats on reading these three tables, stated in the prose above them because they
  differ from the rest of the report. Their denominators are the **full post-treatment
  dataset** for the named objective, taken from `combined_df` rather than the post-filter
  `summaries_mod`, so no sparse treatment × ecoregion combination has been dropped and
  the percentages are not directly comparable with the compiled tables. And they report
  raw positive/negative rates rather than intended/unintended, because a non-target cover
  response has no assigned objective against which a sign could be called intended.*
- ~~How did significant effects change through time, presented in a way we can actually
  talk about (for example, using the time bins discussed above)?~~
  *Addressed: the talkable versions are the prose sentences rather than the raw tables.
  In `_objective_block.Rmd`, chunk `results-X_18` emits the most- and least-effective
  year as sentences; chunk `results-X_19` builds one bullet per effect direction giving
  the peak year, its mean effect, SE and significant-pixel count, flagging the peak as
  censored where relevant; and chunk `results-X_20` provides the 1-5 / 6-10 / 11-15 / 16+
  bin table for the coarser statements. The prose below chunk `results-X_19` notes
  explicitly that the year with the largest mean effect need not be the year with the most
  significant pixels, which is the distinction to keep straight when describing these
  results. The two new compiled figures are the cross-objective versions of the same two
  statements, and they make the contrast concrete: `decrease_tre` has the highest binned
  significance rates of any objective in the report (37.6% in years 1-5, falling to 18.8%
  by 16+), while its largest mean effects fall at years 29 and 31 on 100 and 27
  significant pixels - so the objective with the most reliable detection rate has its
  headline effect sizes in the sparsest part of its record.*
